stem.en: Why does a sodium ion have a charge of exactly +1?

text.en: It has 11 protons but only 10 electrons, so one positive charge is not balanced.
Its nucleus took in one extra proton from chlorine when the bond formed.
Its outer shell is now full, and a full shell always gives a charge of +1.

explanation.en: Charge = protons − electrons = 11 − 10 = +1. Option b is wrong because only electrons move in a chemical change: the nucleus stays the same. Option c is wrong because neon also has a full outer shell, and a neon atom has no charge at all.

hints.en: Count the protons and the electrons in the sodium ion.
